memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then the LORD opened Balaam's eyes, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with his sword drawn. So he bowed low and fell face down. The angel of the LORD asked him, "Why have you beaten your donkey these three times? I have come here to oppose you because your path is a reckless one before me." - Num 22:31-32 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
At last the Lord opens Balaam's eyes, and what he sees brings him to the ground. The angel of the Lord stands before him with a drawn sword. Suddenly Balaam understands: the donkey he beat had actually saved his life three times. He falls face down in fear and shame.

The angel's words cut deep. Balaam's path was "a reckless one" before God. The prophet thought he was pursuing profit and honour; God saw a man rushing headlong into danger. What Balaam viewed as opportunity, God viewed as recklessness. Their perspectives could not have been more different.

This is the mercy of having our eyes opened. Until God gives us sight, we may pursue a course we think is wise, blind to the danger and the divine opposition. But when the Lord opens our eyes, we see reality as it truly is, and often we fall down in humble awe.

We should long for God to open our eyes rather than let us stumble on in blindness. The same God who opened Balaam's eyes gives spiritual sight through Christ, who opens the eyes of the blind (John 9:39). Pray that God would show you where your path is reckless, before the sword is drawn. It is grace to see the truth.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where might you be pursuing a "reckless path" without realising it?
2. Do you ask God to open your eyes to see your situation truly?
3. How has God opened your eyes to something you were once blind to?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, open my eyes to see my ways as You see them. Where my path is reckless, show me before it is too late, and lead me humbly back to You. Amen.
